title: Loss function on the same output
question: Does training with a BER-like loss give a gain over MSE?
git_commit: recorded per run in results/runs/*.json (field git_commit); rule commit: see LOG.md
eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
current_loss: runner.run_task (E010-E029): MSE of the complex symbol |y - s|^2 (complex outputs) or MSE of [I, Q] (real)
loss_notes: logits -beta |y - s_k|^2 over the 16 points, beta = exp(log_beta) trained, initial 1 / mean|rx - tx|^2 of the train files; bit_bce: Gray bits of core.BIT_TABLE; mse+ce = mse + 0.1 ce; decision stays the nearest point

rule_draft.status: DRAFT: to be confirmed by the user before the first run; must not change after results are seen
rule_draft.better: loss L is better than MSE if the difference is >= 0.7 p.p. (5 seeds, intervals do not overlap) on at least two of the four models (S2)
rule_draft.note: E016: linear FIR + own power gave -5 % (worse than raw), a hint that MSE and BER disagree
rule_draft.noise: thresholds in p.p. are compared with results/noise_floor.json (E024): MDD(5 seeds) = t_{0.975,8} * s_pooled * sqrt(2/5); 0.1 dB of Q2 = 6 p.p. at 10 %, 4.1 at 48 %, 3.0 at 66 %, 2.7 at 70 % (anchors); every table prints both
